brief.hook: Here's an unpopular opinion about money that you will not like. Renting is better than owning a house.
keep: A higher price-to-rent ratio means houses cost way more than the average rent, so it often makes more sense to rent and invest the excess. And you want six months of emergency fund minimum, because you'll need a new roof, new AC, all these things.

Renting over owning is sometimes a really smart decision, and not everybody should just buy a house right away. If you're not financially there yet, you might default. Whose fault was that? Your best friend told you to buy that house. Also, if you buy your first house, look into FHA loans. Possible idea. Not recommending.'}

editorPlan.title: Renting beats owning (sometimes)

findings: HOOK_STANDS_ALONE (line 1): The hook is split over three lines (0, 1, 2) with a 0.7 s gap, and line 3 then repeats the thesis ('Rent an apartment is better than owning a house'), so the stance is said twice. → Cut line 3 words 10-19's repeated thesis by trimming it to only 'Now now before you get your panties all on a twist', so the stance lands once.

HEADLINE_PER_BEAT (line 0): The hook headline 'UNPOPULAR OPINION' is a label, not a title a stranger would stop for, and it duplicates the small on-screen tag; the real title is 'RENT > OWN' on line 1. → Headline line 0 'RENT > OWN?' and keep 'unpopular opinion' as the small tag only.

DEPENDENT_LINE (line 4): Line 4 ('Is building your assets… you're not throwing it away') is the counterargument, but cut line 5 ('Yes, of course, owning a house then, right?') was its concession, so the beat trails off without answering it. Line 10 ('when would you rent and when would you buy?') then asks a question the cut never answers directly. → Cut line 10 so the setup ends on line 4 and goes straight into the line 14 tension about a couple of years.

TENSION_ADDS (line 15): Lines 14 and 15 share the headline 'ONLY A COUPLE YEARS?' and line 15 ('Why would you go in a home?') only restates line 14's point, while line 16 carries the new idea (profit risk). → Keep line 14, headline it 'STAYING 2 YEARS?', and merge line 15 into that beat as its punchline question; give line 16 its own headline 'NO PROFIT GUARANTEED'.

NUMBER_IS_PAYOFF (line 36): The six-month figure is buried mid-line in line 36 (word ~17) after the 'completely stupid' line, and line 42 then muddies it with 'three months… three to six months minimum', contradicting 'six months minimum'. → Trim line 42 to end at 'new roof, new AC, all these different things', dropping the three-month clause, and keep 'SIX MONTHS SAVED' as the single headline on line 36.

EMPHASIS_WORDS (line 35): 'stupid' is emphasized on line 35, a harsh blanket judgment that clashes with the 'it's situational' stance and risks shaming buyers; the turn that earns a punch-in is the number or 'best friend'. → Move the emphasis from 'stupid' to 'six' on line 36, or cut line 35 and start the beat at line 36.

ENDING_SERVES_OBJECTIVE (line 54): The last line is 'Good luck.' under a headline 'RENT OR BUY?', so the comment question sits on a throwaway line rather than on a decision, and 'DEFAULT' (line 48) is a downbeat shift from the rent-vs-buy debate. → End on line 53 ('He told you to go buy that house.') with the headline 'RENT OR BUY?', and cut line 54.

COLD_VIEWER (line 44): Line 44 ('renting over owning is sometimes a really smart decision') is a conclusion placed in the middle of the payoff, before the emergency-fund and roof beats, so the video seems to end at ~line 44 and then restarts; a viewer would drift at the 6-months section. → Move line 44 to after line 42 and before line 48 so the conclusion directly precedes the punchline.

editorPlan.rationale: The video takes on 'rent is throwing money away' and lays out the specific situations where renting is the smarter move: a short stay, HOA fees, a high price-to-rent ratio, and no six-month cushion. The 'RENT > OWN?' hook states the stance once, reads with the sound off, and makes viewers pick a side instantly. The payoff lands on the price-to-rent ratio and the six-months-saved rule, then the 'sometimes smart, not if you're not ready' conclusion leads straight into the 'your best friend told you to buy that house' punchline with 'RENT OR BUY?' on screen to pull comments.

storyline.viewerNeeds: A small receipt-style list that ticks in sync with the words: 'new roof', then 'new AC', then '…'. No prices shown.

editorPlan.coldViewer: The stance is said once in the hook, and 'before you get your panties in a twist, it's situational' earns trust within about 8 seconds; the 2-year example follows directly as the first situation, so there is no unanswered question hanging. Each tension beat adds a new reason (short stay, no guaranteed profit, HOA fees, then the ratio), with the HOA jump signposted by its headline change. The six-month rule now stands as one clean number with no conflicting three-month clause, and the roof/AC list explains why. The conclusion 'renting is sometimes smart, not everybody should buy right away, not if you're not financially there yet' now sits right before the default story, so 'And then you default' has a clear referent and the video builds to one ending instead of seeming to finish twice. The likeliest drop point is the ratio explanation around 35-45 s, which the scale graphic must carry; the ending lands on the best-friend line with 'RENT OR BUY?' as the question viewers will answer. Estimated runtime is about 75-80 s from roughly 236 kept words, inside his 60-95 s reference range.
